fact: Document says the Horizon Fiber project, announced in February 2026, is a terrestrial link of nearly 2,800 km extending Djibouti's connectivity into the Horn of Africa; it names no other country and gives no date beyond the announcement.

Ethio telecom, Djibouti Telecom and Sudatel Group converted their December 2024 memorandum into a binding agreement for the Horizon Fiber cross-border terrestrial corridor from Djibouti through Ethiopia to Sudan; the document gives no signing date, so its published date is used.
The three operators signed the Horizon Fiber memorandum of understanding in December 2024.

Ethio telecom, Djibouti Telecom and Sudatel Group signed a binding tripartite agreement at a ceremony in Djibouti to operationalise the Horizon Fiber corridor linking Djibouti's submarine cable gateways through Ethiopia to Sudan; no signing date is given, so the published date is used.

Ethio Telecom, Djibouti Telecom and Sudatel turned their cross-border fibre MoU into a binding agreement for a terrestrial corridor from Djibouti's landing stations through Ethiopia to Sudan; no signing date is given, so the published date is used.
The three telcos signed the original Horizon Fiber MoU in December 2024.

Heads of Djibouti Telecom, Ethio Telecom and Sudatel signed in Djibouti on Wednesday 4 February 2026 the agreement launching Horizon, a terrestrial fibre corridor of nearly 2,800 km with 144 fibre pairs joining Djibouti, Addis Ababa and Port Sudan.
A memorandum of understanding for Horizon was signed in Addis Ababa on 4 December 2024.

TechAfrica News reports that Ethio telecom, Djibouti Telecom and Sudatel signed a tripartite contractual agreement in Djibouti on 4 February 2026 to implement Horizon Fiber, a cross-border optical fibre corridor linking Djibouti's submarine cable landing stations through Ethiopia into Sudan.

BTW Media's 10 September 2026 analysis says the Horizon partners presented the project to prospective users in Addis Ababa (per La Nation, 9 September) and that the report reviewed announces no capacity purchase, paying customer or service start date.

BTW Media states the official announcement of 4 February 2026 describes a multi-terabit terrestrial fibre corridor joining the submarine cable landing stations in Djibouti to those in Sudan via Ethiopia.

SUNA, the Sudanese state news agency, reports Sudatel signed a strategic agreement with Djibouti Telecom and Ethio telecom on 4 February 2026 launching Horizon Fiber, a terrestrial fibre corridor linking Djibouti's international submarine cable stations through Ethiopia to Sudan.

fact: Ethio telecom's press release says it, Djibouti Telecom and Sudatel signed a tripartite strategic agreement on 4 February 2026 under the Horizon Fiber Initiative for a terrestrial fibre corridor joining Djibouti's submarine cable landing stations, across Ethiopia, to Sudan's, building on a memorandum signed in Addis Ababa on 3 December 2024.

La Nation reports that Djibouti Telecom, Ethio telecom and Sudatel signed a tripartite agreement in Djibouti on 4 February 2026 for the construction and maintenance of the Horizon terrestrial cross-border fibre link joining Djibouti, Ethiopia and Sudan.

La Nation reports that the three operators presented Horizon to hyperscalers, carriers and vendors at a pre-commercialisation meeting in Addis Ababa on Monday 7 September 2026, ahead of deployment and commercial launch, so the link was not yet in service.

The Prime Minister told the National Assembly on 1 March 2026 that agreements between Djibouti Telecom, Ethio telecom and Sudatel for a 2,800 km fibre corridor exist, with Horizon Fiber launching to link Djibouti to Ethiopia and South Sudan; no construction is stated.

Data Center Dynamics reports that Ethio Telecom, Djibouti Telecom and Sudatel signed an agreement under the Horizon Fiber Initiative, at an event in Djibouti the week before its 11 February 2026 article, to build a cross-border fibre network linking submarine cable landing stations in Djibouti, Ethiopia and Sudan.
Data Center Dynamics reports the February 2026 agreement builds on a memorandum of understanding the three operators signed in Ethiopia in December 2024 on a secure alternative international route.

Connecting Africa, citing Djibouti Telecom, reports that the DARE1 subsea cable has been operational since 2021 and connects Djibouti City with Bosaso and Mogadishu in Somalia and Mombasa in Kenya, with 36 Tbit/s over three fibre pairs.

ITWeb Africa reports that the DARE1 cable system currently links Djibouti City with Bosaso and Mogadishu in Somalia and Mombasa in Kenya, with 36 Tbit/s over three fibre pairs (published 2025-09-01; no start date given in this document).
TechAfrica News reports that the DARE1 subsea cable system already links Djibouti, Somalia and Kenya (published 2025-09-01; no start date given in this document).

Birr Metrics reports that Ethiopia's Horizon Fiber Initiative is a trilateral agreement with Djibouti Telecom and Sudan's Sudatel to establish a multi-terabit terrestrial fibre link by April 2025; the story gives no signing date, so it is dated by its publication.
